~2 ms of batch prep, then launched forward N+1: a 1.5-2.5 ms GPU idle gap

items.body:

## Overview

When a model emits an empty reasoning block, vLLM drops it from the Responses API output. Clients that send earlier output back as input, like Codex, then replay that turn with no reasoning. This PR keeps the empty reasoning instead.

## Claims

- Non-streaming `/v1/responses` returns an empty reasoning item for an empty reasoning block instead of leaving it out.
- Streaming no longer drops `""` reasoning when it ends in the same delta that starts a tool call.
- `None` still means "no reasoning", so models without reasoning are unaffected.

items.author: ziyixiong-nv
items.summary: When points at a shared filesystem, every rank takes one exclusive lock to load the cache when an session starts, and takes it again to save at the end. Each save reads the whole JSON file, merges, and writes it back with an fsync.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

When `TLLM_AUTOTUNER_CACHE_PATH` points at a shared filesystem, every rank takes one exclusive lock to load the cache when an `autotune()` session starts, and takes it again to save at the end. Each save reads the whole JSON file, merges, and writes it back with an fsync. These calls run between collectives, so a stalled rank stalls all of them. During filesystem trouble, single saves took minutes, the ranks queued behind them, and the autotuner part of startup took close to an hour.

items.body:
Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the
shard writers on other nodes open files in it. On NFS a client that looked the path up before rank 0 created it
can keep that negative lookup cached for a while, so a writer on another node fails to find a directory that
already exists on the server.

_SafetensorShardWriter now calls mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) on every rank that writes shards. The call
goes to the server and refreshes the cached entry; where the directory is already visible it does nothing.

items.title: [RFC]: UltraQuant: the scale constant c = 0.156 is MSE-optimal before the UE8M0 snap, not after; c ≈ 0.2 cuts KV-quantization KL by 40–56% at no cost
items.author: thomaszhang2661
items.summary: Proposes raising the UltraQuant UE8M0 snap scale constant from 0.156 to ~0.20 to reduce post-snap MSE/KL in KV-cache quantization by 40–56% with zero read-side or layout changes.
items.body:
### Motivation.

`ultraquant_4bit` picks each group's UE8M0 scale as

```
s_raw = c * absmax(group)          # c = 0.156 (DEFAULT_CONSTANT_C, vllm/v1/attention/ops/ultraquant/format.py)
s     = 2^round(log2(s_raw))       # UE8M0 snap
```

The constant is documented as "MSE-optimal; `s_raw = c * absmax`, then UE8M0-snapped". That holds before the snap. c = 0.156 minimizes the E2M1 reconstruction error for a **continuous** scale s = c·absmax. But the stored scale is the snapped power of two. items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Fix handshake metadata routing in MultiConnector with pipeline parallelism
items.author: xsxszab
items.summary: Fixes MultiConnector to route per-connector handshake metadata under pipeline parallelism, preventing PP-unaware sub-connectors from rejecting valid initialization.
items.body:
## Overview

`MultiConnector` reports the handshake metadata of the first sub-connector that has any, and passes the engine core's merged `{(pp_rank, tp_rank): metadata}` to every sub-connector. With pipeline parallelism the merged dict has `pp_rank > 0` entries, and a sub-connector without its own `set_xfer_handshake_metadata_pp_aware` rejects them in the base class. So a PP prefill instance that runs NIXL next to a KV store in a `MultiConnector` (e.g. `NixlConnector` + `MooncakeStoreConnector`) fails to start. This PR gives each sub-connector only the handshake metadata it produced.

items.author: DuFanYin
items.summary: Removes incorrect kernel block alignment for slot-mapped token caches that are never splittable, preventing inflated block strides and spurious KV cache memory errors.

## Overview

`customize_attention_spec` aligns the block stride of every spec on a fixed-kernel-block backend to whole kernel blocks, so packed blocks can be split. A packed slot-mapped token cache is never split: `map_kv_cache_to_kernel_blocks` rejects it at binding. items.title: [Perf] [AMD] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: Pack the FP8 GDN input projections on ROCm
items.author: chuyeh
items.summary: Packs FP8 GDN input projections from 4 kernels to 2 on ROCm for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, cutting per-layer decode time from 33.4 µs to 18.5 µs.
items.body:

In Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on MI355X, each of the 36 GDN layers runs its input projection as 2 FP8 quants and 2 FP8 GEMMs (`in_proj_qkvz` and `in_proj_ba`). That is 33.4 µs per layer in the c16 decode profile. The `in_proj_ba` GEMM alone takes 13.8 µs for only 96 outputs.

items.title: Compute DSA split gradient norms from DTensor layouts in FullyShardedOptimizer
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging. The base `get_dsa_split_grad_norms` goes through `get_grad_norm_fp32`, which requires all DTensor gradients to share one mesh, but the non-indexer half mixes dense and expert gradients. `FullyShardedOptimizer` now computes both norms the way its `get_grad_norm` already does, from each gradient's own layout.

A DeepSeek-V4 Pro proxy on 64 GB200 with MFSDP v2 now runs past the first step.

items.title: [Bugfix] Profile the forward again after a profiling pass that compiled
items.author: kxyk99
items.summary: Re-profiles the forward pass after torch.compile resets the allocator peak, preventing undersized KV cache on cold compile caches.
items.body:
## Purpose

On a cold compile cache, `torch.compile` runs inside the first `profile_run()` of `determine_available_memory()`, and its allocator peak is charged as `transient_peak_headroom`. The KV cache is then sized smaller than on a warm boot of the same arguments. items.author: GuoxiangZu
items.summary: Fixes P/D proxies returning application/json instead of text/event-stream for SSE streaming responses, which caused benchmarking tools to silently report incorrect TTFT/TPOT metrics.
items.body:
## Purpose

The P/D proxies forward the decode instance's SSE stream but always label it `media_type="application/json"`. Clients that pick the parsing mode from the `Content-Type` header (e.g. EvalScope `perf`, NVIDIA AIPerf) then treat the stream as a single JSON body: they wait for the whole response, can't parse any tokens, and report

- TTFT = full end-to-end latency
- TPOT = 0, output tokens = 0, throughput = 0

with no error. `vllm bench serve` and the OpenAI Python client ignore the header, so CI didn't catch it. The NIXL toy proxy is referenced in the P/D docs for single-node t

## Summary

This rewrites the `trtllm_modeling_v2` agent flow around one priority: get a HuggingFace checkpoint
answering correctly through the Modeling V2 path as early as possible, and report truthfully what was
and was not done. The goal is a flow that coding agents on weaker models can complete.

- **`onboarded` is decided by code.** The first deployment of the spec (`core`) boots with
  `modeling_v2=require` on a clean committed tree, and each of its benchmarks meets its frozen floor
  (anchor minus two standard errors). With no anchor the run is onboarded on its boot only, and says
  so.

items.author: mawong-amd
items.summary: Adds dedicated ROCm AITER split-KV kernels for speculative-decode verification (GQA 8, head 64, FP8 KV), reducing per-layer decode time by ~2-3x and improving overall p50 decode latency significantly.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

With k draft tokens, each decode request verifies k + 1 query tokens. On `ROCM_AITER_FA` these batches go through AITER `unified_attention`, which dominates the decode step at long context. This PR adds split-KV verify kernels for layers with head size 64 and 8 query heads per KV head, on gfx950 with an FP8 KV cache and 1-7 draft tokens:

- full-attention layers: a FlyDSL kernel with a length-balanced grid, so time tracks total KV rather than the longest request;
- sliding-window layers: a Triton kernel.

The kernels are adapted from sgl-project/sglan

Stop `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator` from re-prefilling a previous request's cached draft inputs when a request slot is reused. Fixes #66886.

items.body:
## Motivation

Part of #48623. This PR covers the Rust TreeCore.

When the KV pool is full of cached prefixes, almost every allocation has to evict something. The Rust core rebuilt its eviction heap from every evictable leaf at the start of each walk, so freeing a couple of pages still cost O(number of leaves). With thousands of leaves that adds up on every decode step.

## Modifications

Instead of rebuilding the heap each time, I keep it around between walks and clean it up lazily:

- `EvictableDeviceLeaves` (new, `evictable_device_leaves.rs`) holds the D-leaf set plus a persistent priority

## Port of #48414

items.title: [sglang-server] Accept client request IDs up to 256 bytes
items.author: lming2001
items.summary: (the Rust frontend) rejects any client-supplied longer than 128 bytes. Callers that namespace their request IDs, such as a caller prefix followed by a UUID or a trace ID, can exceed that, and their requests fail validation with a 400.
items.body:
## Motivation

`sglang-server` (the Rust frontend) rejects any client-supplied `rid` longer than 128 bytes. Callers that namespace their request IDs, such as a caller prefix followed by a UUID or a trace ID, can exceed that, and their requests fail validation with a 400.

## Modifications

- `MAX_RID_LEN` goes from 128 to 256 bytes. The bound still exists because the rid keys the detokenizer table and travels with every streamed chunk.

items.author: wenkaidu
items.summary: Adds custom ring all-reduce and optimized 2shot_push kernels for AMD MI450 (gfx1250) to eliminate RCCL fallback for large all-reduces up to 4 GB in distributed training.
items.body:
Supersedes #49377, which GitHub closed when its base branch (#49370's head) was deleted after #49370 merged. Same five commits, rebased onto main; the earlier review and discussion are on #49377.

## Motivation

On MI450 (gfx1250), carv2's 2shot_push sends almost the whole tensor across the fabric twice, and the per-vector kernel waits after every scoped store. Above a few MB it loses to RCCL, so large all-reduces (prefill chunks, large-batch decode) fell back to RCCL. This PR adds two gfx1250-only paths so carv2 can take every size up to 4 GB at TP2-8, and tunes the size table for both kernel

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Honor a processor-level frame cap when profiling Qwen3-VL videos
items.author: subhashpolisetti
items.summary: Fixes Qwen3-VL video profiling dummy builder to respect processor-level `cap_pixels_per_frame` instead of only reading from `videos_kwargs`, matching the full video token budget.
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

items.title: [#22150][fix] Register RPC response futures before sending requests
items.author: itsrayeedscodespace
items.summary: A regular RPC reply can reach while is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout.
items.body:
## Description

Fixes #22150.

A regular RPC reply can reach `_handle_regular_response` while `_call_async` is still awaiting the transport send. The response future is currently registered only after sending, so the reader discards that reply and the caller waits indefinitely with the default timeout. Remote errors can be lost in the same way.

Register the future under the existing admission/close lock before sending. Include the send in the existing `try/finally` so send failures and caller cancellation remove the registration. Fire-and-forget calls still send without allocating a response

items.author: ekagra-ranjan
items.summary: When torchcodec is installed but its FFmpeg core can't be loaded, every call retries the load and logs a warning before falling back to soundfile. This PR remembers that failure for the rest of the process.
items.body:
## Overview

When torchcodec is installed but its FFmpeg core can't be loaded, every `load_audio` call retries the load and logs a warning before falling back to soundfile. This PR remembers that failure for the rest of the process. items.title: [RFC]: int8-key / int4-value per-token-head KV cache dtype (between int8 and int4)
items.author: jramirez-uab
items.summary: Proposes a mixed-precision k8v4_per_token_head KV cache dtype combining int8 keys with int4 values for better quality/memory tradeoff than uniform quantization.
items.body:
### Motivation.

The per-token-head family has `fp8`, `int8` and `int4`. Keys and values do not tolerate 4 bits equally: the attention scores depend on the keys, while the values average out over many tokens. An int4 cache loses most of its quality in the keys. Storing the keys as int8 and keeping the values at 4 bits recovers most of it for 392 bytes per (token, KV head) at head size 256, against 264 (int4) and 520 (int8, fp8).

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Take the INT4 value zero-point sum on the rounded P
items.author: jramirez-uab
items.summary: Fixes INT4 attention precision drift by computing the zero-point sum on the same rounded P_v operand as the dot product, reducing relative error from 28% to 0.4% at long contexts.
items.body:
## Purpose

`_attn_packed` (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/int4_per_token_head.py`) computes `acc += tl.dot(P_v, V) - sum(P_v * v_zp)`. Both operands of the dot are fp32, which Triton rounds to TF32, but the zero-point sum is taken on the unrounded `P_v`. The rounding error is multiplied by a zero point of about 8 and does not cancel, so the output drifts away from the true attention and gets worse with the context length.

`prefill_schedule_interval=N` defers prefill to every Nth engine step, so decode-only steps sit between prefill chunks. items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `bool`/`int`/`float`/`str`

items.author: raghavc

## Overview

Fixes #67065. With `NixlConnector` in pull mode, a decode request with `n > 1` gets split into `n` children that all read the same prefill request, but the prefill frees that request's blocks after the first child's notification. Children that finish reading later can decode from blocks another request has already reused. This makes the prefill wait for all `n` children.

## Claims

- For a P/D decode request with `n > 1`, the prefill keeps its KV blocks until every child has read them, so no child reads reused blocks and the prefill logs no `Potentially invalid KV blocks` error

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Make MoRIIO READ wait for pending KV block zeroing and copies
items.author: kliuae
items.summary: Fixes a race in MoRIIO READ mode on ROCm where async compute-stream zeroing/copying could overwrite received KV cache blocks before the decoder reads them.
items.body:
## Overview

With a mixed-precision KV cache (e.g. DeepSeek-V4) and async scheduling, MoRIIO READ mode can lose prompt KV it has already received, as the model runner zeroes new blocks on the compute stream and nothing orders MoRI's writes after that. This PR makes the decode worker wait for the compute stream before its first read whenever that stream still has zeroing or block copies queued for the step's READ destinations.



## Claims

- Received KV is written only after the compute stream has finished zeroing and copying the destination blocks.
- That fixes the accuracy drop. On MI355X

With the extensible KV cache (#56492), the default on CUDA and ROCm, `gpu_memory_utilization` defaults to 1.0 and the KV cache is sized from the memory measured after warmup. items.author: sshleifer
items.summary: Fixes a memory leak in the static KV cache allocator where failing to allocate from one of two pools (full attention or SWA) would discard the already-allocated page from the other pool.
items.body:
## Codex notes

### Motivation

The static allocator has two separate memory pools: one for full attention and one for sliding-window attention (SWA). A decode that crosses a page boundary needs a new page from both.

Allocation happens separately:

1. Full allocates a page successfully.
2. SWA is full, so its allocation fails.
3. The combined operation returns `None`, but does not return the Full page it already took.

The decode fails while still consuming memory. The reverse can also happen: Full allocation fails, but the code still allocates an SWA page and loses it.

### What does this PR do?

Adds a TileLang fused linear cross-entropy output head and integrates it with FSDP, Megatron, and VeOmni training. The TileLang path supports multi-label/top-k log probabilities, including repeated labels, so distillation and score-centering losses can consume precomputed student top-k log probabilities without materializing full logits.

This also extends the SFT and separate-async OPD CI matrices to exercise TileLang under FSDP/SP and Megatron TP/SP/PP/CP configurations while retaining non-fused baselines.

items.author: CiaranCw
items.summary: With, a secondary-tier hit is first promoted (copied) into the CPU primary tier and only then loaded into the GPU. The tiering metrics count promotions and their bytes, but not whether a promoted chunk was ever used.
items.body:
## Overview

With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a secondary-tier hit is first promoted (copied) into the CPU primary tier and only then loaded into the GPU. The tiering metrics count promotions and their bytes, but not whether a promoted chunk was ever used. This PR records, for each chunk a promotion lands, exactly one outcome: `loaded`, `served_peer`, `evicted_unloaded` or `reset`. It also records the time from landing to that outcome, the chunks still waiting for one, and promotions started again for chunks that were evicted unread.

items.body:
## Overview

Add --all2all-backend mooncake, backed by Mooncake EP's ElasticBuffer, which follows the DeepEP v2 API and runs on CUDA and XPU. It reuses DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize with two adaptations:

- combine() takes no allocate_on_comm_stream argument.
- In expand mode Mooncake still returns a recv_topk_idx tensor that its kernels leave unfilled; drop it so the expert ids are rebuilt from the per-expert token counts.

Wire MooncakeAll2AllManager into the CUDA and XPU communicators and use the PaddedStandard activation format, as for deepep_v2.  has_mooncake_ep() checks the parent package

items.title: [Fix] Z-Image: Correct and optimize Ulysses sequence layout
items.author: avjves
items.summary: Z-Image has 30 attention heads, which do not divide evenly across Ulysses degree 8. Its spatial SP planner also rounds each local image shard to a multiple of 32, even when the complete image already meets the model's 32-token alignment.
items.body:
## Motivation

Z-Image has 30 attention heads, which do not divide evenly across Ulysses degree 8. Its spatial SP planner also rounds each local image shard to a multiple of 32, even when the complete image already meets the model's 32-token alignment. At 1088x1920 this adds 32 attention-visible image tokens that the single-device reference does not require. The main transformer stack additionally treats caption tokens as a replicated suffix in every block.

This PR adds model-local head padding, a guarded global-alignment path, and joint image/caption sequence sharding for native eager Ulysse

items.title: [Feat] offloader: Let OffloaderV1 offload only the model-declared submodule
items.author: Vegetog
items.summary: Models tell the offloader which submodule of each layer to offload through. OffloaderV2 honors it, but OffloaderV1 ignores it and always offloads whole decoder layers until the budget is used up.
items.body:
## Motivation

Models tell the offloader which submodule of each layer to offload through `offloader_kwargs` (`submodule_accessor`). OffloaderV2 (`--offload-group-size`) honors it, but OffloaderV1 (`--cpu-offload-gb`) ignores it and always offloads whole decoder layers until the budget is used up.

Whole-layer offload breaks models that use layer parameters outside the layer's `forward`, which V1's `functional_call` wrapper does not cover. With DeepSeek-V4 (after #49850 adds its `offloader_kwargs`), `--cpu-offload-gb 110` fails while loading, because the mHC parameters were moved to CPU:

FP8 draft KV caches can require larger physical pages than an already aligned TurboQuant/Mamba hybrid target cache. This can inflate the shared page size and cause engine startup to fail when splitting padded cache pages.

items.summary: Switches Muse Spark fused rmsnorm from FlashInfer's Cake backend to CuTe DSL to fix a PDL race that corrupts hidden states and produces garbage outputs at DP+EP with TP=1.
items.body:
## Overview

Run Muse Spark's `gated_residual_rmsnorm` on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL backend instead of the default Cake backend. The Cake programs for 128 rows or fewer read `branch` before `griddepcontrol.wait` (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9343). This corrupts the hidden states that DSpark reads, so DSpark output is garbage at DP + EP with TP=1. No open PR addresses this.

## Claims

- Fixes DSpark at DEP8: AIME25 0% → 98.9%, GSM8K 23.1% → 94.8%, sdAL back to 3.7–3.9.
- No end-to-end perf change at TEP4.

## Validation

B300, Muse Spark NVFP4 + DSpark (7 draft tokens), FP8 KV.

**DEP8 accuracy**

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix M-RoPE position preparation when PCP is enabled- #66516
items.author: baolongsun
items.summary: Fixes incorrect 3D M-RoPE position computation under PCP by adding a PCP-aware path in RopeState, restoring PCP2 accuracy parity with TP2 for multimodal models.
items.body:
Added a new method to prepare M-RoPE positions for a PCP-local batch, handling both prefill and regular requests.



### Overview
This PR fixes M-RoPE position preparation under PCP for multimodal models.
PCP splits one request into rank-local fragments, but the original RopeState.prepare_positions() assumed a 1:1 mapping between local rows and global requests. For M-RoPE models, this produced incorrect 3D positions, especially for image inputs. This PR adds a PCP-aware path that reconstructs the correct 3D positions for each local fragment.
### Claims
- Fixes incorrect M-RoPE position

## Overview

With a block-outermost KV cache layout (`VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`), every layer's page of a block sits in one contiguous row, but NixlConnector still registers one region per layer for full-attention (GQA) caches. items.author: apex-mochen
items.summary: Fixes indefinite delay in KV-cache `AllBlocksCleared` event delivery after prefix cache reset by emitting it immediately instead of deferring to the next scheduler step.

`Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache()` clears the block pool immediately, but the resulting `AllBlocksCleared` event was only drained by `_publish_kv_cache_events()` at the end of the next `update_from_output()`. This is a liveness fix for the event path, not a change to the reset semantics.

## Description

Kimi K3 multi-node serving on GB300 occasionally received a corrupted host broadcast: a cross-node receiver of `safe_broadcast` got a payload with one contiguous span of wrong bytes. items.summary: The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device.
items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

items.author: buptzyb
items.summary: , the bookkeeping kernel of the batch-invariant Mamba decode, reads the slot's write cursor in every thread of a program and has one thread store the advanced cursor at the end. The threads of a Triton program are not synchronized with each other, and the kern…
items.body:
## Summary

`_decode_step_prep_kernel`, the bookkeeping kernel of the batch-invariant Mamba decode, reads the slot's write cursor `num_buffered[slot]` in every thread of a program and has one thread store the advanced cursor at the end. The threads of a Triton program are not synchronized with each other, and the kernel launches with four warps. A warp that reaches the load after that store uses the advanced cursor and copies its elements of the token's x / dt / B / C rows into the next buffer row (row 0 after a crossing).

The row that the scan then reads keeps the values of one chunk earlier

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. # What does this PR do?

Hypercorn wraps an `fd://` bind in a socket object of its own and closes it when `serve()` returns, and the server then closes the same descriptor again (`own_socket.close()`), which logs `OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor` from every frontend at shutdown and could close an unrelated descriptor. This PR passes `os.dup(own_socket.fileno())` to hypercorn, so each owner closes its own descriptor.

items.author: xie-tj

items.title: [vllm, hardware] feat: allow sleep level 2 with vllm-ascend >= 0.30.0
items.author: lxb007981
items.summary: Older vllm-ascend versions have an EP precision issue with sleep level 2 that can cause rewards to collapse to zero. Restrict the NPU sleep level 1 guard to vllm-ascend < 0.30.0, while preserving the MTP and LoRA guards.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Older vllm-ascend versions have an EP precision issue with sleep level 2 that can cause rewards to collapse to zero. This is fixed in v0.30.0.

Restrict the NPU sleep level 1 guard to vllm-ascend < 0.30.0, while preserving the MTP and LoRA guards.

Compare sleep levels 1 and 2 in an experiment based on: tests/special_npu/nightly_ci_ascend/run_grpo_glm52_top16_megatron_npu_multinode.sh

items.author: lauradang

items.body:
## What

A hybrid (Mamba) engine with TP > 1 and EP = 1 (e.g. TP=2, EP=1) can crash with `No free recurrent-state slots for 1 expert-parallel dummy request(s)`.

The engine's work consensus runs over the `tp_ep` group (expert TP x EP), and between refreshes it reuses a cached result. After local work drains, the stale cache can still say "there is work", so the engine runs a dummy forward. That dummy forward needs a recurrent-state slot, but the dedicated dummy slot was only reserved for EP > 1. On a prefill engine whose slots are all held by pending KV handoffs, allocation fails.

**The fix.*

### What does this PR do?

Allow colocated NPU rollouts to explicitly select vLLM-Ascend's native IPC loading lifecycle. The trainer packs bounded byte buffers, exports a fresh IPC reference for each nonempty bucket, and waits for the worker to finish consuming that bucket. Leaving the option unset preserves the existing CUDA/ROCm, shared-memory and delta dispatch paths.

This is part 1 of a three-PR series: IPC, HCCL, then whole-stream reload.

items.title: [ray] fix: prevent master port races during worker startup
items.author: SeptPonts
items.summary: Prevent during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore. Previously, probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Prevent `EADDRINUSE` during Ray worker startup caused by the gap between selecting a master port and binding PyTorch's TCPStore.

Previously, `RayWorkerGroup` probed a free port with a temporary socket, closed it, and passed the port to workers. Another process could claim that port before rank zero initialized its process group.

Rank zero now binds and retains the actual TCPStore before invoking the user worker constructor. It publishes the bound endpoint before that constructor can block waiting for peers, allowing the driver to start the remaining ranks.

items.title: Fix math_dapo Minerva extraction for markdown-decorated answers
items.author: siddhant-rajhans
items.summary: The existing regex captures the markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0. Fixes #8449 ## Root cause The Minerva answer pattern matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line.
items.body:
## Bug

Models commonly wrap the Minerva `Answer:` label in markdown bold/italic (`**Answer:** 42`, `Answer: **42**`, `**Answer:**\n\n42`). The existing regex captures the `*` markers as part of the answer, so correct answers score -1.0.

Fixes #8449

## Root cause

The Minerva answer pattern `(?i)Answer\s*:\s*([^\n]+)` matches the literal "Answer" and captures everything after the colon to end of line. When models decorate with markdown:

| Input | Extracted | After normalize | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| `**Answer:** 42` | `** 42` | `**42` | -1.0 |
| `Answer: **42**` | `**42**` | `**42**` |

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

items.author: 0z5a

## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: Hardens the weight push from the Megatron trainer to the vLLM rollout engines, for both the IPC (colocated) and the NCCL (distributed) updater. This is the first of the smaller PRs announced in #478 after closing #479, and it is independent of FSDP2.
items.body:
## Summary

Hardens the weight push from the Megatron trainer to the vLLM rollout engines, for both the IPC (colocated) and the NCCL (distributed) updater. This is the first of the smaller PRs announced in #478 after closing #479, and it is independent of FSDP2.

1. **Time out weight-transfer requests.**
   - New flags:

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. ## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

items.body:
## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Includes @aoshen02's local multi-turn smoke test (aoshen02/vime#4) with his agreement, then makes the loop actually train on ROCm/MI355X.

## Why it couldn't train

The smoke test runs end to end but cannot learn on any platform:

```
--n-samples-per-prompt 1
--rollout-temperature 0.0
```

GRPO computes its advantage within a prompt's sample group. One sample gives an advantage of identically zero; greedy decoding makes n samples identical, so group variance is zero too. Both have to change — fixing either alone still gives no gradient.

## What's in here

items.body:
## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.
